newsitem.title: UK: FKI duly nods Newman Tonks TESA sale.
newsitem.headline: FKI duly nods Newman Tonks TESA sale.

text.p: British engineering group FKI Plc slammed bid target Newman Tonks Group's sale of a one-third stake in Spanish firm TESA to Williams Holdings, but said shareholders had no choice but to vote in favour.

"Newman Tonks' board has left shareholders with no choice but to rubber-stamp a dilutive disposal...the board of FKI reluctantly concludes that Newman Tonks shareholders should vote in favour" of the disposal, a statement said.

FKI, which has already received acceptances for over 20 percent of its target, said Newman Tonks had failed to exploit pre-emption rights on the remainder of TESA and criticised "poison pill" provisions introduced in the sale on trading arrangements in the event Newman Tonks was taken over.
It said the sale would be "highly dilutive" to Newman Tonks' earnings.
It criticised BZW, advisers to Newman Tonks, for not providing independent financial advice on the TESA transaction in a document earlier this month.
"Newman Tonks' management continues to demonstrate the shortcomings which have led to five years under-performance," FKI chairman Jeff Whalley said in a statement.
FKI launched its hostile 195.7 million stg bid for Newman Tonks in December 1996 and has extended the deadline for acceptances until 1500 GMT on January 24.
